Definition: from G303 and G2578; to turn back:--(re-)turn.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to turn back, to return: the wise men, warned of God in a dream not to return to Herod, departed into their own country another way, and Hebrews says the patriarchs, if they had been mindful of the country they came out of, might have had opportunity to have returned. It is the turning back that obedience refuses and homesickness invites.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for turning back carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two turnings — the wise men who would not go back to Herod, and the fathers who would not go back to the country they had left.
